clue.text: Block of stone in coalpit oddly disappearing in a few weeks

indicators.note: in places the surviving letters of the pit word within the period of time

parts.note: a month is a period of about four weeks

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions vanish, leaving only the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A mysterious stone block turns up at a coal mine and is gone within weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly disappearing' strips the odd letters of COALPIT, leaving OLI, which goes 'in' MONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single large standing stone, such as those at prehistoric sites.

clue.text: Courtyard, where first of crew lost

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the team word as the one to go
lost says that opening letter is dropped from the team word

parts.note: a crew or team is a squad

explanation.surface: A courtyard where the leading crew member went missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A quad, short for quadrangle, is an enclosed courtyard, as in a college.

clue.text: See 22 across
Weapon on fire, launched in fight

indicators.note: in puts the burning word inside the scrap word

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: in a down entry something launched is sent up, so the burning word is read upwards

parts.note: something on fire is lit

explanation.surface: A flaming weapon is hurled in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launched' reverses LIT to TIL, because in a down clue something sent up reads backwards; it goes 'in' SET-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Certainly rare, yet tragic past

parts.note: certainly as a reply means yes

indicators.note: tragic suggests something wrecked, so the letters of the two words are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual but sorrowful history, the clue says with conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragic' is the anagram signal; 'past' looks like an adjective but is the noun, the bygone time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear is a literary word for times gone by, the bygone days.

clue.text: Drink for a man? Relative of Isaac, say

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
brew is a drink, such as beer or tea

explanation.surface: A drink meant for a man, and a question about a kinsman of Isaac.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'he-brew', a drink for a male. Isaac, son of Abraham, is a Biblical patriarch, so any of his people is a fair example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrews are the ancient Israelite people descended from Abraham, so one of them is kin to Isaac.

clue.text: Senior on back end of dinosaur in TV show

indicators.note: on places the pensioner after the creature's rear part
back end of keeps only the rear part of the long-necked beast, cutting off its front

parts.note: the diplodocus is a long-necked dinosaur
a senior citizen is an OAP, old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An old person sits on a dinosaur's rump on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back end of' trims DIPLODOCUS to DOCUS. OAP, old-age pensioner, is British for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: A docusoap is a fly-on-the-wall documentary series following real people like a serial.

clue.text: See 24
Winners detailed in ancient city

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with the final letter cut off

parts.note: the winners are the best

explanation.surface: Victors are described in detail in the history of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means tail removed: THE BEST loses its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Egypt, and another of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Artist missing article in least satisfactory glossary

indicators.note: in places the trimmed painter's name within the word for poorest

parts.note: the least satisfactory is the worst

indicators.note: missing says the article is taken out of the painter's name

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a Surrealist artist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A painter is absent from the poorest reference list.
explanation.walkthrough: DALI 'missing' A gives DLI, which goes 'in' WORST.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical register of terms with their meanings.

clue.text: Good to shave hairy back, twisted or plaited, initially

indicators.note: initially says the jumbled letters come first, before the final piece
twisted signals that the letters of the two words are wound into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: back picks the rear letter of the word hairy

explanation.surface: Advice that something is good for shaving a hairy back, whether tangled or braided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' is the anagram signal, 'back' takes the last letter of hairy, and 'initially' puts the jumbled letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A depilatory is a cream or treatment that removes body hair, so it is suited to the job of a razor.

clue.text: Just beaten — like apples?

definitions.meaning: to be narrowly defeated, as at the post
apples contain pips, so they are full of seeds

explanation.definitionFit: Pipped means beaten by a whisker, and fruit that has pips is pipped in a punning sense.

clue.text: Competitor breaking record in mucky film?

indicators.note: breaking means the record splits the phrase for dirty coating in two

parts.note: poo is mucky stuff, excrement
a film is a thin layer
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A contestant smashes a record in a grubby movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mucky film' is read as POO LAYER, a coating of excrement, and LP comes 'breaking' it. Pool is the cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool player is a contestant in the cue sport of pool, someone who competes at the table.

clue.text: Headbutt PM in dark

parts.note: to nut someone is British slang for headbutting them
Gordon Brown was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Someone headbutts the Prime Minister in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'nut' is British slang for a headbutt; Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut-brown describes a dark, warm brown shade like a hazelnut's shell.

clue.text: Leaders in race on Arctic trek caught by your old husky

indicators.note: caught by means the initials are held inside the archaic possessive

parts.note: thy is an old form of your

indicators.note: leaders in takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Sled dogs leading a race across the Arctic belong to you, in old-fashioned speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders in' gives ROAT, 'caught by' THY. 'husky' looks like the sled dog of the surface but is the adjective for a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is deep and rough, the same quality as a throaty one.

clue.text: Cloth wiping head from below before massaging under nipple

indicators.note: in a down entry under places the jumbled letters beneath the teat word

parts.note: a teat is a nipple

indicators.note: massaging works the remaining letters around into a new order
wiping head from removes the first letter of the word below

explanation.surface: Instructions for a cloth: wipe, then massage beneath a nipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiping head from' turns BELOW into ELOW, 'massaging' rearranges it to OWEL, and 'under' puts that below TEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel is a kitchen cloth for drying washed dishes.

clue.text: Flipped ball catches me going the wrong way

indicators.note: catches means the testicle word holds the turned pronoun inside it

parts.note: a ball in slang is a testicle, a gonad

indicators.note: going the wrong way says the two letters of me are read backwards

explanation.surface: A ball comes back at me and I catch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' turns ME into EM, which GONAD 'catches'. 'Flipped' is not a reversal signal but the slang for losing one's temper or sanity.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is slang for losing control, so someone who has flipped has lost their mind.

clue.text: Prayer used, gain converts

indicators.note: converts says the letters are changed into another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Religious converts take up a prayer for their own benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' rearranges USED GAIN; it looks like a noun for new believers but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is a prayer said or sung in the Mass.

clue.text: Girl filling empty shoes, slippers?

indicators.note: filling puts the girl's name in the hollow footwear
empty strips the inside out of shoes, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl tries on someone's vacant shoes, which might be house slippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' shoes gives S and S, and 'filling' puts KATE between them. The question mark flags 'slippers' as things that slide, not house shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates glide across ice, so they are things that slide along, playfully called slippers.

clue.text: Waste container and lifting mechanism getting a nut turned round?

definitions.note: the words a nut read backwards spell the fish tuna

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for building waste, in Britain
a jack is a device for raising heavy loads such as a car

explanation.surface: A bin and a car jack are used to turn a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British name for a builder's large waste bin. The definition is itself a play: 'a nut' reversed is TUNA, and the skipjack is a kind of tuna.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipjack is a species of tuna, the fish spelt out by reading the clue's two words backwards.

clue.text: Tricky, describing wading bird?

definitions.meaning: a tricky problem is complicated and hard to solve
the knot is a wading bird of the sandpiper family, so something like one could be called by its adjective

explanation.definitionFit: Knotty means intricate and puzzling, and playfully it is also the adjective of the knot, a shorebird.

clue.text: Able to bounce back well, like billionaires?

parts.note: a spring is a natural well or water source
loaded is slang for very rich

explanation.surface: Rich people are said to be resilient and good at recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' is the noun, a water source, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-loaded part has a spring that pushes it back into place after being pressed.

clue.text: Just like that, a crimson rose

parts.note: so means in that way, just like that
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Simply put, a red rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Soared and rose both describe going up high, as a bird does in flight.

clue.text: Back-stabbing braggart, son a sociopath controlling family

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read from right to left
stabbing pierces into the run of words, finding letters lodged inside them

explanation.surface: A treacherous show-off, a son with no conscience, running a crime clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'stabbing' look like one word for betrayal, but split into two signals: reversed and lodged inside braggART SON A SOCiopath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian Mafia is called by this Italian name, meaning our thing, a crime syndicate dominating its territory.

clue.text: See 10
Possible killer on board, clue so hot?

parts.note: a lead is a clue in an investigation
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: A clue so hot it might reveal the killer at the game board.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead piping is one of the murder weapons in the board game Cluedo, a whodunit game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cluedo the culprit may have used a length of lead pipe as the weapon, so it could kill.

clue.text: Goddess soon afterward in hospital department?

indicators.note: in places the time word within the hospital unit

parts.note: A and E is the Accident and Emergency department of a British hospital
then means soon afterward, next

explanation.surface: A goddess shows up shortly after in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E, Accident and Emergency, is the British casualty department; THEN goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, also spelt Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Rocked — Neptune's slayer, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is as heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Neptune is the Roman god of the sea, so his killing weapon is fancifully a sea sword

explanation.surface: Something rocked, and rumour links it to the killer of Neptune.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'sea sword' and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To see-saw is to move up and down or back and forth, just as something rocking does.
